message:
Hello MD. RAFIQ,

I intend to sell a vehicle security report as a commercial PDF product and am looking for a designer who can help me finalise it.

The written content, sample report structure, scoring system, and example report versions are already prepared. It assesses theft risk for high-value vehicles, giving each customer a risk score and category together with a breakdown of weaknesses and recommended security actions.

Would you be able to assist with this?

Hello Caleb,

This is a project I can help you with. Using my experience in professional report and PDF design, I can turn your existing content, scoring system, and structure into a polished vehicle security assessment suitable for commercial use.

Clear risk scores and categories can be combined with structured findings, recommendations, professional visual elements, and a consistent branded layout that customers can easily read and understand.

Once you share the current report files, sample versions, and any branding requirements, I will review the materials and recommend the best approach.

Kind Regards,
Rafiq Mahmud

Thanks for replying.

To clarify the scope, I need the existing report transformed into a polished, premium, editable template that looks and feels like a professional paid assessment. Because the report content already exists, this is not a full copywriting assignment; the focus should be its design, layout, structure, and editability.

The main requirements are as follows:

\- Front-page results panel

A prominent score/dashboard panel should appear on the first page. It must display the customer's vehicle security score, risk band, exposure level, priority level, main reason for the rating, and primary weaknesses, allowing the customer to understand the result immediately upon opening the report.

\- Consistent page furniture

Every page needs a clean, consistent header and footer containing the report name, report ID, vehicle group, confidential/restricted status, assessment date, and page number.

\- Transparent scoring summary

Please include a clear table listing the main scoring categories, maximum score, customer score, and total score so the assessment appears transparent and professional.

\- Action-led upgrade path

Rather than being purely informational, the recommendations should be practical and clearly prioritised, ideally as immediate actions, priority upgrades, and secondary upgrades.

\- Fully editable templates

Editability is essential because I will update the reports for different customers. Fields that I need to change include the vehicle registration, assessment date, report ID, vehicle group, security score, risk band, category scores, weaknesses, recommendations, and customer-specific notes.

\- Several report variants

Please create editable versions for DX17, DX18, DX19, and DX20 so I can choose the appropriate template according to the customer's score or risk level.

The completed files must be straightforward to edit and export as a PDF. Canva or PowerPoint may be the best option, although I am open to another format if you recommend something more suitable.

Could you please confirm:

\- Whether you can help with this type of project
\- Which file format you recommend
\- What materials you need from me before beginning
\- The estimated cost
\- The estimated timescale
\- Whether all fonts, icons, and design assets required for future editing will be included in the final files

Once I know the project is a good fit, I can send the existing sample report and any reference images.

Thanks

Yes, this project is a very good match for the work I provide.

For the primary editable format, I recommend Microsoft word or InDesign because either will provide strong flexibility when updating scores, vehicle details, and recommendations, while also supporting the export of high-quality PDFs. A Canva version can also be supplied if you prefer.

Before work begins, please provide:

1\. The existing report and sample versions
2\. Any branding assets, including the logo, colors, and fonts
3\. Any reference examples or design preferences, although I can develop the design idea as well
4\. Details of the DX17–DX20 report variations

All final templates will be fully editable and will include the fonts, icons, and design assets needed for future updates.

After all materials have been received, the estimated timeline is 8–12 business days. An accurate cost can be provided once I have reviewed the current report and confirmed the scope.

Please send the sample report and reference materials when ready; I will review them and then prepare a detailed proposal.

Kind Regards,
Rafiq

Hi,

Thank you for sending over the updated report design. The overall direction is much stronger now, and I'm happy with the general look and feel, so I do not want to redesign it from scratch.

I would like to make a final round of refinements to improve readability, consistency, and the overall commercial finish before I sign it off.

The main changes I'd like are:

1\. Make the front-page score more dominant.

Please make the "67/100" score slightly larger and give it more breathing room so it feels more like the main dashboard result. The customer should immediately notice the score and risk outcome when they open the report.

2\. Rename "Security Score" to "Vehicle Security Score"

On the front page, please change the heading from "Security Score" to "Vehicle Security Score" to make it feel more complete and professional.

3\. Simplify the "What Caused This Result" section.

The wording is good, but the dark blue panel currently feels quite text-heavy. Please reduce this section into shorter, easier-to-scan bullet points. For example:

\- No independent immobilisation
\- No circular steering lock
\- No live-location tracking
\- Storage location is being overvalued
\- Owner security habits reduce protection

The longer explanation can remain elsewhere in the report if needed. Still, page one should feel more immediate and easy to read.

4\. Remove placeholder text

Please remove any placeholder text such as "Click to enter a date." This should either be replaced with the actual assessment date or a clean editable placeholder such as "\[Assessment Date\]".

5\. Check report code consistency

Please check that the report code is consistent throughout. I noticed some areas may show "AC-47". This should be "DX-17" throughout unless there is a specific reason for using something different.

6\. Clean up the vehicle group section

The checkboxes next to Range Rover / Range Rover Sport / Defender make the section feel slightly like a form rather than a completed report. Please either make this a cleaner fixed line, such as:

"Vehicle Group: Range Rover / Range Rover Sport / Defender"

or make it customer-specific, for example:

"Vehicle Assessed: Range Rover Sport"

7\. Add a subtle header to pages 2 onwards

The footer works well, but I'd also like a subtle header across the internal pages for consistency. Something simple would be fine, such as:

"Vehicle Theft Risk Assessment | DX-17 | Confidential"

This should be subtle and not take up too much space.

8\. Refine the red distribution warning on the final page

I like the idea of the warning section, but the red block currently feels a little too heavy. Please keep the warning, but make it slightly more refined and less visually dominant, while still making it clear that the report is confidential and for limited distribution.

Overall, I'm happy with the design direction. I want this final round to focus on polish, readability, consistency and making the report feel like a premium paid assessment.

Please let me know if the above changes are clear and when you expect to send the revised version.

Thanks
